critical_code_review_comments: /app/frontend/src/lib/global-font.ts:26-36 — Correct fix. Injecting `style: [props?.style, { fontFamily }]` into `nextProps` BEFORE origRender.call means the array is resolved by RN-Web's own StyleSheet.flatten inside the Text renderer, so React DOM only ever receives a serialised className/inline-style object. No more setValueForStyle('0') crash. Guard `if (!flat.fontFamily)` correctly leaves explicit icon-font families (Ionicons, FontAwesome) untouched. The try/catch fallback to `props` is defensive and appropriate.

rca_of_issue: Iteration 25 root cause was that applyGlobalFont() used React.cloneElement to add fontFamily AFTER Text.render already returned, wrapping the DOM element's style in an array which React DOM tried to assign via element.style[0] = ... (throws 'Failed to set an indexed property [0] on CSSStyleDeclaration', unmounting the subtree). Fix in iteration 26: the patch now mutates the incoming `props` object before origRender.call, so the array becomes an INPUT to RN-Web's Text renderer instead of a POST-render mutation to a DOM node. RN-Web internally StyleSheet.flatten()s the array to a single className/inline-style pair for React DOM, so no indexed-property write ever occurs. Verification: 0 CSSStyleDeclaration errors across 8+ page navigations, /pings /encounters /profile /nearby /forgot-password all render non-empty, and getComputedStyle(el).fontFamily on visible text returns Quicksand-Bold / Quicksand-SemiBold / Quicksand-Regular (never the system stack). No further mitigation required.
